desc.concept: Mixed fragments: code identifiers, prose words and subword pieces, no shared theme
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous (Ds, U, PH, film, guests, tag, Richards, message, video, oscillator, underscore, possessive s, Candidates, could, Nano, password, process, comma); no single concept covers them and the windows span unrelated domains.

desc.concept: scattered unrelated word tokens across varied academic and news text
desc.note: Marked tokens share no common concept; windows span medical, legal, news and science text with no single shared feature.

desc.concept: the word "is" after a problem noun ("the problem is")
desc.note: Only 8 of 19 windows mark " is"; the rest are scattered unrelated tokens (suffers, remains, error, to, some, in, etc.), so the concept covers under half.

desc.concept: dotted/punctuation-joined code identifiers and member accesses
desc.note: Marked tokens are a mix of code identifiers and member-access fragments; the most consistent pattern is a code identifier or dotted/slashed member name.

desc.concept: color words and color-related tokens in code and text
desc.note: Activation is scattered across unrelated tokens with no shared concept; color appears in only 4 windows and no dominant family emerges.

desc.concept: code and text fragments; no single shared concept
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous: code syntax (context, hosts, null, sensor, string), punctuation, and prose words. No concept covers 45% of windows.

desc.concept: Mixed code/text tokens: boilerplate license and code block boundaries, no single topic
desc.note: Windows are heterogeneous (Go code, license headers, Norwegian/Danish news, Docker output); the 'compliance' tokens recur but only 4 of 20 windows, below the 25% threshold for a token-level concept.

desc.concept: mixed unrelated word fragments and tokens; no shared concept
desc.note: Windows span unrelated domains (microbiology, engineering, math, Brazilian forestry, celebrity news) with no common token or context; the marked tokens are scattered word fragments and single characters.

desc.concept: scattered tokens with no shared concept
desc.note: Marked tokens are mostly function words and punctuation across unrelated documents; no single feature covers them.

desc.concept: period after a title abbreviation (Dr., Mr., Ms., Prof.)
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous: 9 periods, plus honorific/title tokens (Ms, Dr, Prof, Sergeant, Super, Figure, ices, Station, Chef, Figures). Concept covers the largest group only.

desc.concept: scattered unrelated tokens with no shared pattern
desc.note: Marked tokens span code, citations, legal text, emails, dating ads and more; no single concept covers them.

desc.note: Marked tokens are varied fragments across computing, sports, finance and prose; only the 'co' prefix (co-processors, co-workers, co-processors) recurs, in 3 of 20 windows.
